name: Rania Haddad
headline: 28, part-time university tutor and freelance translator, Amman
title: A Walk Around the Campus Gardens
situation: After her last class, Rania packs her satchel and heads toward the bus stop. As she passes the faculty lounge, a fellow writing instructor, Samir, calls out from the doorway. He says he's seen her grading in the courtyard and asks if she'd like to join him for a quick walk through the campus gardens before she leaves. It's unusually pleasant weather, and he mentions he has something to ask about the department's reading list. Rania has a stack of essays to mark tonight and a translation deadline, but the offer is simple and unhurried. She pauses and considers whether to say yes.

context.relationship_profiles:
Samir is a fellow adjunct writing instructor she has known for two years; they share lesson ideas and occasionally cover each other's office hours.
He is one of the few colleagues who has never treated her contract status as a reason to dismiss her, and she respects his judgments about course materials.
Once after a late department meeting, he offered her a ride home; she accepted, then repaid him by reading a set of his student drafts.
context.tendencies:
When an invitation conflicts with grading or translation deadlines, she has usually declined and offered a rain check, suggesting a specific later time.
When a colleague raises a pedagogical question she finds interesting, she has sometimes stayed despite unfinished work, especially when the conversation felt collaborative.
On warm afternoons, she has occasionally taken short walks between classes to clear her head, though she rarely initiates them.
context.current_state:
She is physically tired from three back-to-back classes, and her satchel feels heavy with unmarked essays.
She has not slept well for two nights because of translation deadlines, and her eyes sting when she looks at screens.
Her jacket pocket holds a prefilled bus card and a folded list of essay comments she still needs to write.
context.immediate_memories:
Samir's mention of the reading list brings back the department meeting where he argued for adding a contemporary Arab essayist, and she had silently agreed.
Passing the faculty lounge reminds her of the afternoon he found her grading in the courtyard and brought her a cup of tea, saying she looked like she needed it.
The gardens' jasmine near the gate reminds her of evening walks with her grandmother, who loved to recite lines of Arabic poetry aloud.
context.reflective_memories:
She remembers that before her divorce, she stopped accepting invitations because her ex-husband resented time spent outside the house; since returning to Amman, she has deliberately said yes to simple colleague offers.
During her own graduate years, her most useful teaching insights came from informal bench conversations with professors, not from official office hours.
She has learned that a colleague's question can sharpen a syllabus or open a new translation assignment, but it also pushes her evening schedule later.
